speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to determine the underlying cause, are these lesions painful or painless, and do they have a specific shape or pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to captopril and meloxicam.

The combination of new-onset cutaneous blisters and severe mucosal ulcers (oral and genital) in a patient who recently started captopril and stopped meloxicam is highly suggestive of a severe cutaneous adverse reaction. Given the history of hiking, I also want to rule out Rickettsial infection. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, Urinalysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the forearm blisters and oral/genital ulcers.
